punctuated:
老于漢，佛于晉宋齊梁之間，而無或喪焉者也。非不能喪也，心之根於人人者，自不能喪也。故學者由是而學焉，以得乎其本心之正，則理常矣而弗邪，教貞矣而弗異，政達矣而弗悖，文粹矣而弗雜，道一矣而弗二，物治矣而弗亂，倫若矣而弗拂，行昭矣而弗違，德備矣而弗賊。由是盡性以至於命，而天下之能事畢矣。
自夫經殘教弛，而心學不講，徒求之於言語之粗，而不知其爲明德之實功；濟之以功利之私，而不知措而爲躬行之實事。是故拘之名數，則有若王弼；泥之訓詁，則有若鄭康成、孔穎達；擬而續之，則有若王仲淹；因文說理，則有若蘇軾、陳少南；語涉空幻，則有若張子韶。夫空幻，妄也；文詞，藝也；擬而續，僭也；訓詁，淺也；名數，末也。五學出而六經之道晦矣。董仲舒明於春秋，天人之對似矣，而縱陽閉陰之說，則失之誕；京房長於易學，□□
translation_en:
…the teachings of Huang-Lao in the Han, and Buddhism during the Jin, Song, Qi, and Liang, yet it was never lost. This was not because it could not be destroyed: what is rooted in the heart of every person cannot of itself be lost. Thus, when learners study by this means and attain the rectitude of their original heart, principle becomes constant and free from deviation; teaching becomes correct and free from heterodoxy; government becomes effective and free from perversity; writing becomes pure and free from admixture; the Way becomes unified and free from division; affairs become ordered and free from disorder; human relationships become harmonious and free from discord; conduct becomes illustrious and free from transgression; and virtue becomes complete and free from injury. By this means, they fully realize their nature and thereby reach an understanding of Heaven’s mandate, exhausting all that can be accomplished under Heaven.
Ever since the classics were damaged and teaching grew lax, the learning of the heart has gone undiscussed. People have sought it merely in the superficialities of language, without recognizing that it is the substantive work of making bright virtue manifest. They have supplemented it with selfish calculations of achievement and profit, without knowing how to put it into actual personal practice. Thus, among those who confined it to names and numerical categories was Wang Bi; among those who became mired in textual glosses were Zheng Kangcheng and Kong Yingda; among those who imitated and continued the classics was Wang Zhongyan; among those who expounded principle through literary composition were Su Shi and Chen Shaonan; and among those whose language strayed into emptiness and illusion was Zhang Zishao. Emptiness and illusion are delusion; literary composition is an art; imitating and continuing the classics is usurpation; textual glosses are shallow; and names and numerical categories are peripheral. With the emergence of these five approaches to learning, the Way of the Six Classics became obscured. Dong Zhongshu understood the Spring and Autumn Annals, and his responses concerning Heaven and humanity seemed sound; yet his doctrine of giving free rein to yang and shutting off yin erred in extravagance. Jing Fang excelled in the study of the Book of Changes, [two illegible characters: □□]…

title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
賢之論似矣而不密失身則失之愚張禹
為帝師而不能抑外戚之專卒成王氏之
禍何取於經術乎胡廣位台輔而不能正
清河之位遂養閹竪之亂何取於鉅儒乎
夫失之誕者其心罔失之愚者其心蔽而
張禹胡廣則患得患失而溺焉者也三患
生而六經之道塞矣鄭夾漈曰秦火焚書
而書存諸儒窮經而經絕豈非有感而言
者歟自夫經學不明民心易惑於他岐風
===
俗不淳異端遂起而鼓之是故李耳著道
德經以倡清淨之教而迂誕譎恠之徒競
為異說以濟其妄故言煉養則有若赤松
子魏伯陽言服食則有若盧生李少君言
符籙則有若張道陵寇謙之言經典科教
則有若杜光庭林靈素轉相流布而其說
始蔓延無極矣漢明帝遣蔡愔使天竺求
佛經以倡釋氏之教而迷惑昏昧之輩靡
然景慕以習其法故楚王英之於沙門吳

賢之論似矣，而不密失身，則失之愚。張禹為帝師，而不能抑外戚之專，卒成王氏之禍，何取於經術乎？胡廣位台輔，而不能正清河之位，遂養閹竪之亂，何取於鉅儒乎？夫失之誕者，其心罔；失之愚者，其心蔽；而張禹、胡廣則患得患失而溺焉者也。三患生，而六經之道塞矣。鄭夾漈曰：「秦火焚書而書存，諸儒窮經而經絕。」豈非有感而言者歟？自夫經學不明，民心易惑於他岐，風俗不淳，異端遂起而鼓之。

…his discussion of the worthy seemed sound, yet through a failure to keep matters secret he brought ruin upon himself: his failing was folly. Zhang Yu served as the emperor’s teacher but could not restrain the monopoly of power exercised by the imperial consort’s relatives, ultimately bringing about the calamity of the Wang clan. What value, then, was there in his classical learning? Hu Guang occupied the highest ministerial rank but could not set right Qinghe’s position [?], thereby allowing the disorder wrought by eunuchs to grow. What value, then, was there in his standing as a great Confucian scholar? Those whose failing was extravagant speculation had deluded minds; those whose failing was folly had obstructed minds. Zhang Yu and Hu Guang, however, were consumed by anxiety over obtaining office and fear of losing it. Once these three afflictions arose, the Way of the Six Classics was blocked. Zheng Jiaji said: “The Qin fires burned the books, yet the books survived; the scholars exhaustively studied the Classics, yet the Classics were lost.” Surely these words sprang from deeply felt concern! Once classical learning became obscure, people’s minds were easily led astray onto other paths; customs lost their integrity, and heterodox teachings arose to stir people up.

Thus Li Er wrote the Classic of the Way and Virtue (Daode jing) to promote the teaching of purity and stillness. Followers given to extravagant, deceptive, and strange notions competed to devise divergent doctrines that would further their delusions. Thus, among those who discussed refining and nourishing the self were Chisongzi and Wei Boyang; among those who discussed ingesting substances were Lu Sheng and Li Shaojun; among those who discussed talismans and registers were Zhang Daoling and Kou Qianzhi; and among those who discussed scriptures and ritual teachings were Du Guangting and Lin Lingsu. They circulated these teachings from one to another, until their doctrines began to spread without limit.

…Sun Quan’s relationship with Senghui, Fu Jian’s with Shi Dao’an, and Yao Xing □ in relation to Yongming and Kaihuang [?]: they vied in transmitting and expounding these teachings, until their writings became a hundred times more numerous than the Six Classics. Cao Can followed the arts of Huang-Lao and thereby brought about government characterized by purity and stillness. Yet Emperor Huizong of the Song, though he styled himself Lord of the Dao, ultimately could not avert the disaster of the Jingkang era. The purity and stillness taught by Laozi already departed from the balanced and correct Way of the sages and worthies; what Huizong studied, moreover, lost even Laozi’s essential meaning. Setting up a curtained enclosure to lecture on scriptures and conferring a title of Jade Purity—what purpose did these serve? Liu Qizhi grasped the import of spiritual insight and thereby understood the boundary between life and death. Yet Emperor Wu of the Liang, who offered up his own person in service to the Buddha, could not escape the peril at Taicheng. Buddhist quiescence and extinction already departed from the former kings’ principles concerning the mind and human nature; what Emperor Wu studied, moreover, misconstrued even the essential meaning of Buddhism. ‘As the Way rises, demons grow stronger; as one does good, obstructions arise’—what sort of claim is this? Han Yu said: ‘Make their people ordinary people, burn their books, and turn their dwellings into homes.’ Was it not because these teachings deceived the people and deluded the world that he repudiated them?

title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
治人之術將躋天下生民於壽域豈獨一
已之長生久視哉苟一受其獻則迂誕恠
妄之士必爭來矣此其崇正闢邪以立萬
世之極者至矣我
皇上明物察倫優入聖域垂敬一之訓衍四箴
之義以布之學宮正孔子先師之號抑廣
孝配享之非禮樂之舉天地爲昭此其明
道弘化以續帝王之統者至矣天下之士
若民亦罔不曉然趨經術之正而知異端
===
之弊也夫何鉛槧之士抱藝以進者乃弗
良於經世緩急之際尚或有乏才之憂緇
黃之流規利而食者乃攘臂於四方明哲
之賢猶不免尊信之失有識者所以隱憂
而浩嘆也愚則以爲士之所以不獲實用
者其病有三曰詞章也富貴也功利也而
三者之中詞章之害爲先民之所以趨於
異端者其病有三曰惑也懼也貪也而三
者之中惑之害爲先何也古者以鄉三物

translation_en:
…the arts of governing people. I intend to bring all the people under Heaven into a realm of longevity. How could I seek long life for myself alone? If I were once to accept such an offering, men of outlandish, fantastic, and deluded claims would surely compete to come forward.” Thus his exaltation of orthodoxy and rejection of heterodoxy, establishing a supreme standard for all ages, reached the highest degree!
Our present Emperor discerns the nature of things and examines human relationships, attaining the realm of sagehood with ease. He has bestowed his Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness and elaborated the meaning of the Four Admonitions, distributing these teachings to the schools. He has rectified Confucius’s title as First Teacher and rejected the impropriety of Guangxiao’s receiving associated sacrifices. His measures concerning rites and music shine clearly before Heaven and Earth. Thus his clarification of the Way and extension of moral transformation, carrying forward the succession of emperors and kings, have reached the highest degree! Scholars and common people throughout the realm alike clearly turn toward the orthodox learning of the Classics and recognize the evils of heterodox teachings.
Why, then, do men who wield the writing implements and advance through their literary accomplishments prove inadequate to ordering the world, so that in times of urgency there is still sometimes anxiety over a lack of talent? Why do the black-robed and yellow-robed clergy, who seek profit to sustain themselves, act boldly throughout the land, while even wise and discerning worthies cannot avoid the error of revering and trusting them? This is why those with understanding harbor deep concern and sigh profoundly.
In my humble view, scholars fail to prove useful in practice because of three failings: devotion to literary composition, wealth and rank, and achievement and gain. Of these three, literary composition does the greatest harm. The people turn toward heterodox teachings because of three failings: delusion, fear, and greed. Of these three, delusion does the greatest harm. Why is this? In antiquity, through the three categories of instruction in the local districts…

title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
教萬民而賓興之而今之科目則惟以文
藝故童而習焉長而學焉父兄之所教焉
師友之所講焉有司之所取焉非是弗趨
是故學者涉經傳裂章句以藻飾組繪曰
是足以取青紫矣曰是足以致顯名矣而
不復致力於身心道德之理及出而服諸
官政也則所用非其所學見之不明不能
不移於功利守之不定不能不流於富貴
矣噫聖人作經所以教人淑諸身心而達
===
之用也顧以為利禄之資哉古者析言破
律亂名改作執左道以亂政者則誅而今
之異教罔知禁絕故荒幻之說得以塗民
耳目佛氏曰世界為幻性命為欲秉彝為
妄老氏曰無為為宗慈儉為行虛無為用
於是不知者從而惑之故報應影響幽冥
刑獄之說得以懼之而後有禮土木以祈
免禍患者矣超凡入聖飛昇變化之術得
以誘之而後有罄囊家以徼福利者矣噫

教萬民而賓興之，而今之科目則惟以文藝。故童而習焉，長而學焉，父兄之所教焉，師友之所講焉，有司之所取焉，非是弗趨。是故學者涉經傳，裂章句，以藻飾組繪，曰：「是足以取青紫矣。」曰：「是足以致顯名矣。」而不復致力於身心道德之理。及出而服諸官政也，則所用非其所學，見之不明，不能不移於功利；守之不定，不能不流於富貴矣。噫！聖人作經，所以教人淑諸身心而達之用也，顧以為利禄之資哉？

古者析言破律、亂名改作、執左道以亂政者則誅，而今之異教罔知禁絕，故荒幻之說得以塗民耳目。佛氏曰：「世界為幻，性命為欲，秉彝為妄。」老氏曰：「無為為宗，慈儉為行，虛無為用。」於是不知者從而惑之，故報應影響、幽冥刑獄之說得以懼之，而後有禮土木以祈免禍患者矣；超凡入聖、飛昇變化之術得以誘之，而後有罄囊家以徼福利者矣。噫！
translation_en:
…to instruct all the people and honor the worthy as guests before recommending them for advancement. Today’s examinations, however, judge solely by literary skill. Thus people practice it as children and study it as adults; fathers and elder brothers teach it, teachers and friends discuss it, and the responsible officials select candidates by it. They pursue nothing else. Consequently, students skim the classics and commentaries, tear apart their chapters and sentences, and weave them into ornate literary embellishments. They say, “This is enough to obtain the blue and purple robes of office,” and “This is enough to win an illustrious name.” They no longer devote themselves to the principles of moral cultivation in body and mind. When they enter official service and undertake administration, what they must use is not what they have learned. Without clear understanding, they cannot help turning toward expediency and personal advantage; without firmness in their convictions, they cannot help drifting toward wealth and rank. Alas! The sages composed the classics to teach people to cultivate goodness in body and mind and put it into practice. Could they instead have intended them as resources for securing profit and official emoluments?

In antiquity, those who split hairs over words to subvert the statutes, confused established terms and introduced unauthorized innovations, or practiced heterodox arts to disrupt government were put to death. Today, however, no one knows to prohibit and eradicate heterodox teachings, so their wild and illusory doctrines are allowed to befoul the people’s ears and eyes. The Buddhists say, “The world is illusion; human nature and life are desire [?]; the constant moral nature is delusion.” The followers of Laozi say, “Nonaction is our guiding principle, compassion and frugality our practice, and emptiness our means of operation.” Those who lack understanding follow these teachings and are led astray. Thus doctrines of retribution following deeds like shadows and echoes, and of punishments and prisons in the underworld, can frighten them. Then there are those who bow before clay and wooden images, praying to escape calamity and suffering. Arts promising to transcend the ordinary and enter sagehood, ascend into the heavens, and undergo transformations can entice them. Then there are those who empty their purses and exhaust their household resources [?] to seek blessings and benefits. Alas! …

title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖人綱常之道所以扶持人紀計安天下
也顧可違之以自入於夷狄禽獸之域哉
曰然則科目可盡廢乎曰何可廢也君子
在道不在制曰然則將盡比今之異端而
誅之乎曰何可誅也百姓從好不從令夫
道者制之本也苟用之以道則今之制猶
古之制也又何患乎人才之不足而詞章
之爲病耶朱子曰非是科舉累人自是人
累科舉耳夫好者令之本也苟率之以正

無邪慝矣然則道豈多乎哉好豈遠乎哉
亦曰明乎六經之常而不失其本心之正
焉爾雖然操轉移之機以神天下之化則

聖人綱常之道，所以扶持人紀、計安天下也，顧可違之以自入於夷狄禽獸之域哉？曰：「然則科目可盡廢乎？」曰：「何可廢也？君子在道，不在制。」曰：「然則將盡比今之異端而誅之乎？」曰：「何可誅也？百姓從好，不從令。」夫道者，制之本也。苟用之以道，則今之制猶古之制也，又何患乎人才之不足而詞章之爲病耶？朱子曰：「非是科舉累人，自是人累科舉耳。」夫好者，令之本也。苟率之以正，則上有好者，下必有甚焉者矣，又何患乎民俗之未善而異端之爲害耶？孟子曰：「君子反經而已矣。經正，則庶民興；庶民興，斯無邪慝矣。」然則道豈多乎哉？好豈遠乎哉？亦曰明乎六經之常，而不失其本心之正焉爾。雖然，操轉移之機，以神天下之化，則固有聖君賢相在也。

第五問
translation_en:
The sages’ Way of the cardinal bonds and constant virtues sustains human relationships and provides for peace throughout the realm. How could one turn against it and thereby enter the domain of barbarians and beasts?

Someone asks: “Then may the examination system be abolished entirely?” I reply: “How could it be abolished? The gentleman’s concern lies in the Way, not in institutional forms.” Someone asks: “Then should all be classed with today’s adherents of heterodox teachings and executed?” I reply: “How could they be executed? The common people follow the preferences of those above them, not their commands.”

The Way is the foundation of institutions. If present institutions are employed in accordance with the Way, they are like those of antiquity. Why then worry that talented men will be insufficient or that literary composition will become a harmful pursuit? Master Zhu said: “It is not the examinations that burden people; people themselves burden the examinations.” The preferences of those above are the foundation of commands. If they lead through upright preferences, then whatever those above favor, those below will inevitably favor still more strongly. Why then worry that popular customs have yet to become good or that heterodox teachings will cause harm? Mengzi said: “The gentleman merely returns to the constant norms. When these norms are set right, the common people are stirred to virtue; when the common people are stirred to virtue, there will be no depravity or wickedness.”

Does the Way, then, require so many things? Are the preferences required so far beyond reach? It is simply a matter of understanding the constant principles of the Six Classics and preserving the rectitude of one’s original heart. Nevertheless, as for grasping the crucial means of bringing about change and making the realm’s moral transformation wondrously effective, there are indeed a sagely ruler and worthy chief ministers to do so.

Fifth Question

text:
駱騰霄
同考試官教諭覃批二法一立兵農兩
得其利誠王政急務也但對者多勦陳言不顧
問意是作獨能發之且識見高議論確深得謀
國之道可以觀子用世矣
考試官左贊善張批屯田鹽法國之大利
出焉而今日之弊則不可言矣是作能究悉弊

同考試官教諭覃批：「二法一立，兵農兩得其利，誠王政急務也。但對者多勦陳言，不顧問意。是作獨能發之，且識見高，議論確，深得謀國之道，可以觀子用世矣。」

考試官左贊善張批：「屯田、鹽法，國之大利出焉，而今日之弊則不可言矣。是作能究悉弊端，而興利之術鑿鑿可行，其經世之才也歟！」

考試官右諭德倫批：「此議行，則立事立功者無嫌於自力矣。錄之。」

一言而王覇異者，功利是也。《書》稱：「利用厚生，九功惟叙。」先王治天下，豈以功利爲諱哉？而後世儒者則始羞稱之。夫所惡乎言利之臣者，爲其蔑棄政教，而顓以剥下媚上爲也。飲食之人，則人賤之矣，而天下豈有不飲不食之人哉？舉天下飲且食焉，而斯人者獨謂之飲食之人，其必有謂矣。《記》曰：「生財有大道。」又曰：「不畜聚斂之臣。」聚斂
translation_en:
Luo Tengxiao

Associate Examiner Qin, Instructor, comments: “Once these two systems are established, soldiers and farmers alike will benefit. This is indeed an urgent task of kingly government. Yet most respondents merely plagiarize stale formulations without attending to the question’s intent. This essay alone brings that intent to light. Its insights are lofty and its arguments sound; it profoundly grasps the way to plan for the state. From it one can see how you would put your abilities to use in public service.”

Examiner Zhang, Left Assistant Adviser, comments: “Agricultural garrisons and the salt administration yield great benefits for the state, yet their present abuses are beyond telling. This essay thoroughly investigates the sources of those abuses, and its methods for promoting benefits are demonstrably practicable. Surely its author has a talent for statecraft!”

Examiner Lun, Right Mentor, comments: “If this proposal is implemented, those who accomplish undertakings and achieve results will have no cause for misgivings about exerting themselves. Select it.”

What distinguishes the kingly way from the hegemonic way in a single expression is ‘achievement and profit.’ The Book of Documents declares: ‘Make resources useful and enrich the people’s livelihood; let the nine achievements be duly ordered.’ When the former kings governed the realm, did they regard achievement and profit as forbidden subjects? Only later Confucian scholars began to feel ashamed to speak of them. What is detestable about ministers who speak of profit is that they discard government and moral instruction, devoting themselves exclusively to exploiting those below and flattering those above. People despise a person devoted to eating and drinking; yet is there anyone in the world who neither drinks nor eats? Everyone in the world drinks and eats, but this person alone is called ‘a person devoted to eating and drinking’: surely there is a particular reason for this designation. The Record of Rites says, ‘There is a great way to produce wealth.’ It also says, ‘Do not retain ministers who exact wealth from the people.’ Ministers who exact wealth…

title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之臣覇之下者也生財之道王道也不講
生財之道其勢必至於畜聚斂之臣夫既
不畜聚斂之臣而又不講夫生財之道則
吾未知其何以為國也王者以民為天民
以食為天王政之所當厚者莫先於農而
費農以養者莫甚於兵兵不可去則凡可
以為兵食地者莫不為之周慮而遠圖之
故夫屯田鹽法之始興也凡以厚農也蠻
夷猾夏宼賊姦宄自唐虞不能免而秦漢
===
===
盛時邊郡轉輸之費或三十鍾而致一石
生民之病不亦大可哀耶鹽之領於官也
以杜兼并之源也其通之於商也以布上
下之利也其中之于邊也以省任載之煩

punctuated: 之臣，覇之下者也；生財之道，王道也。不講生財之道，其勢必至於畜聚斂之臣。夫既不畜聚斂之臣，而又不講夫生財之道，則吾未知其何以為國也。王者以民為天，民以食為天。王政之所當厚者，莫先於農；而費農以養者，莫甚於兵。兵不可去，則凡可以為兵食地者，莫不為之周慮而遠圖之。故夫屯田鹽法之始興也，凡以厚農也。蠻夷猾夏，宼賊姦宄，自唐虞不能免；而秦漢盛時，邊郡轉輸之費，或三十鍾而致一石。生民之病，不亦大可哀耶？鹽之領於官也，以杜兼并之源也；其通之於商也，以布上下之利也；其中之于邊也，以省任載之煩也。山陝之民，僦牛車，具徒伍，奔走顛踣於風雪山谷之中，而無救於待哺之期。曾平時豐歲，室家不相保；一有兵荒之警，上廑宵旰之憂，亟發內帑以濟之，乃至無從得粟。則知實邊生財，豫濟變圖負急而飛輓之□□
translation_en:
…such ministers stand below even those who practice the way of the hegemon; the way of producing wealth is the kingly way. Unless the means of producing wealth are studied, circumstances will inevitably lead to retaining ministers who exact wealth from the people. If one neither retains such ministers nor studies the means of producing wealth, I do not know how one can govern a state. The king regards the people as Heaven; the people regard food as Heaven. Among the things that kingly government should foster, none takes precedence over agriculture; among those whose maintenance consumes agricultural resources, none exceeds the army. Since the army cannot be dispensed with, every possible means of providing a basis for its food supply must receive comprehensive consideration and long-term planning. Thus, when military agricultural colonies and the salt regulations were first established, their purpose throughout was to strengthen agriculture. The Man and Yi disturbing the Chinese realm, bandits, robbers, and evildoers within and without—these could not be avoided even under Tang Yao and Yu Shun. Yet during the flourishing times of Qin and Han, the cost of transporting supplies to the frontier commanderies sometimes amounted to thirty zhong of grain for a single shi delivered. Is not this suffering of the common people deeply pitiable?

Salt was placed under official control to cut off the source of monopolistic accumulation. Merchants were allowed to trade in it so that its benefits might circulate among those above and below. Salt contracts were awarded at the frontier to spare the trouble of hauling supplies. The people of Shanxi and Shaanxi hired ox carts and assembled teams of laborers, rushing about and stumbling through wind and snow in mountain valleys, yet still could not meet the needs of those awaiting food. Even in peaceful times and years of abundant harvest, households could not keep themselves secure. Once war or famine threatened, His Majesty was burdened with cares that kept him working from before dawn until late at night, and urgently disbursed funds from the palace treasury to provide relief; yet matters could reach the point where grain was nowhere to be obtained. Thus one understands the importance of provisioning the frontier and producing wealth, of preparing to meet unforeseen crises, and of planning [?] for urgent transport of supplies—the final wording is unclear, with two illegible characters…

title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
莫過於鹽糧也鎮守之兵徧天下屯田亦
徧天下諸軍更番迭休率以十分之三服
農畝之事一人受田四十畝歲入十二石
足供一兵而自食其餘餘丁則亦以差受
田而歲課其入立法之初以為承平日久
則餘丁益多而地利益盡充拓得人則增
屯益廣而歲入益增如是而兵無加額焉
行之百年舉天下之屯糧足以盡廩天下
之兵而民糧之上供者惟上之所用之耳
===
乃今升斗之給盡出民力一兵以上悉仰
縣官然後知屯田之不可以已也漢文帝
所以能賜民田租者徒以募民入粟實邊
次實郡縣而京師自有餘耳然而酬民以
爵啓鬻官之漸孰若開中之法酬商以鹽
使民得食味商得取贏兩利而無害乎唐
府兵之所以稱近古者徒以兵皆土著而
不廩於官也然而籍農為兵或至業務交
廢孰若屯田之法兵以餘力治農服勤舊

punctuated:
莫過於鹽糧也。鎮守之兵徧天下，屯田亦徧天下。諸軍更番迭休，率以十分之三服農畝之事。一人受田四十畝，歲入十二石，足供一兵而自食其餘。餘丁則亦以差受田，而歲課其入。立法之初，以為承平日久，則餘丁益多，而地利益盡；充拓得人，則增屯益廣，而歲入益增。如是而兵無加額焉，行之百年，舉天下之屯糧，足以盡廩天下之兵，而民糧之上供者，惟上之所用之耳。
乃今升斗之給，盡出民力；一兵以上，悉仰縣官，然後知屯田之不可以已也。漢文帝所以能賜民田租者，徒以募民入粟實邊，次實郡縣，而京師自有餘耳。然而酬民以爵，啓鬻官之漸，孰若開中之法，酬商以鹽，使民得食味，商得取贏，兩利而無害乎？唐府兵之所以稱近古者，徒以兵皆土著，而不廩於官也。然而籍農為兵，或至業務交廢，孰若屯田之法，兵以餘力治農，服勤舊
translation_en:
…nothing surpasses the exchange of salt for grain. Garrison troops are stationed throughout the realm, and military agricultural colonies likewise extend throughout it. The troops take turns rotating off duty, with, as a rule, three-tenths engaged in farming. Each man receives forty mu of land, yielding twelve shi of grain annually—enough to provision one soldier, with the cultivator eating the remainder himself. The additional adult males in military households likewise receive land in graded allotments, and their annual deliveries are assessed. When this system was first established, it was expected that, as peace continued, these additional males would grow more numerous and the land’s productive capacity would be more fully realized. If capable men were entrusted with expansion, the colonies would become more extensive and annual receipts would increase. If this continued for a hundred years without increasing the authorized troop strength, the grain from military colonies throughout the realm would suffice to provision all its soldiers. Grain contributed by the civilian population would then be available solely for the sovereign’s use.
Yet now every sheng and dou of provisions comes entirely from the people’s labor; every soldier depends on the government. Only then do we recognize that military agricultural colonies cannot be dispensed with. Emperor Wen of Han was able to remit the people’s land tax simply because he encouraged them to deliver grain, first to fill the frontier granaries and then those of the commanderies and counties, while the capital naturally had a surplus. Yet rewarding the people with ranks of honor opened the way to the sale of offices. How could that compare with the kaizhong system of rewarding merchants with salt for their grain deliveries, enabling the people to season their food and merchants to earn profits, benefiting both without harm? The reason the Tang militia system was praised as approaching ancient practice was simply that its soldiers were all locally settled and received no provisions from the government. Yet registering farmers as soldiers sometimes led to the neglect of both occupations. How could that compare with the military agricultural colony system, under which soldiers use their spare strength to farm and labor diligently … [the final character 舊 is doubtful here: ?]

title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
惰自食其力兩利而無害乎二法立□
國無餘計豈不誠然乎哉夫不知立法之
源則不知行法之委不知立法之利則不
知廢法之害夫鹽者以竈爲本以商爲用
二者皆優恤所當加也今郡縣無勸農之
政則鹽司豈復有恤竈之實哉商人罰賑
而費出無經草蕩之弗清流亡之不復則
給散亦豈能均適哉姑如河東顆鹽幾年
而遇時風結花倍常乃亦拘守常額不聽
===
撈辦是猶粒米狼戾而封其倉庾俾之棄
於塗泥之中曾不得爲遺秉滯穗其於勸
相阜康之道從可知矣國初征商甚薄而
酬估甚厚是以商人樂趨邊而無變計以
其家衆占閒田稍役屬其民而耕之以待
國之開中之事故私積亦富而粟價亦平
邇者粟貴徵粟粟賤徵銀重之以勸借之
科罰困之搭配之守支展轉折閱業荒衆
散一有控訴則有司且以奸商罔利罪焉

惰，自食其力，兩利而無害乎？二法立□，國無餘計，豈不誠然乎哉？夫不知立法之源，則不知行法之委；不知立法之利，則不知廢法之害。夫鹽者，以竈爲本，以商爲用，二者皆優恤所當加也。今郡縣無勸農之政，則鹽司豈復有恤竈之實哉？商人罰賑，而費出無經；草蕩之弗清，流亡之不復，則給散亦豈能均適哉？姑如河東顆鹽，幾年而遇時風，結花倍常，乃亦拘守常額，不聽撈辦，是猶粒米狼戾而封其倉庾，俾之棄於塗泥之中，曾不得爲遺秉滯穗。其於勸相阜康之道，從可知矣。

國初征商甚薄，而酬估甚厚，是以商人樂趨邊而無變計，以其家衆占閒田，稍役屬其民而耕之，以待國之開中之事，故私積亦富而粟價亦平。邇者粟貴徵粟，粟賤徵銀，重之以勸借之科罰，困之搭配之守支，展轉折閱，業荒衆散。一有控訴，則有司且以奸商罔利罪焉。
translation_en:
…indolence [?], and support themselves by their own labor: does this not benefit both sides without harming either? Once these two systems are established [□], the state needs no further measures—is this not truly so? Those who do not understand the origins of a law’s establishment do not understand the ramifications of its implementation; those who do not understand the benefits of establishing it do not understand the harm of abandoning it. Salt production rests upon the salt-making households and operates through merchants. Both deserve favorable treatment and relief. If prefectures and counties now have no policies to encourage agriculture, how can the salt administration still provide actual relief to salt-making households? Merchants are penalized with compulsory contributions for famine relief, and expenditures follow no fixed rules. The reed marshes remain uncleared [?], and those who have fled do not return: how, then, can distributions be equitable and appropriate? Take, for example, the granular salt of Hedong. After several years, a timely wind may come and produce twice the usual quantity of salt crystals; yet officials cling to the regular quota and forbid its collection. This is like sealing the granaries when grain lies scattered in abundance, leaving it to be discarded in the mud, without even allowing it to serve as sheaves and ears left for gleaners. From this one can judge their approach to encouraging and assisting production and bringing prosperity and well-being.

At the beginning of the dynasty, levies on merchants were very light and their remuneration very generous. Merchants therefore gladly went to the frontier and had no thought of changing their plans. They used members of their households to occupy idle land, gradually engaging local people under their direction to cultivate it, in readiness for the state’s system of exchanging grain deliveries for salt certificates. Thus private grain reserves were plentiful and grain prices stable. Recently, however, when grain is dear, the authorities demand grain; when grain is cheap, they demand silver. They compound these burdens with assessments and penalties imposed under the guise of soliciting loans, and distress merchants through compulsory allocations and waits to receive their salt [?]. Repeated losses erode their capital; their enterprises fall into neglect and their people disperse. Whenever they lodge a complaint, the responsible officials go so far as to condemn them as unscrupulous merchants seeking illicit profit.

title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
商固四民之一而職利之趨也將使皇皇
求仁義乎商不近利是農不望秋也且買
窩者奸商也而賣窩者誰耶不誅怯將而
誅怯兵兵益不精不誅賄吏而誅賄民賄
益不止法弊而售奸良商亦奸奸懲弊革
奸商亦良人才與時奸良而況商乎別奸
恤良無以掊克之政一施之則善矣若夫
括餘鹽之利則京帑雖實而邊郡增糴運
之煩加引目之數則商利益微而勤竈夫
補恤之惠若是者無乃論列愈詳而鹽法
愈不通耶屯政之不綜也始傷於嚴而卒
壞於寬也因習之故非一日矣自父祖侵
而有之而子孫固以為巳世業也雖左驗
甚明至死不心服若是則雖有必行之政
安得而加哉富豪乾沒而告訐横行雖明
者或不能辨則仁者固不欲棘之也番休
之法不行兵久駐屯依憑威虐兵實病民
田屯相遠形勢勢格兵不得田民亦病兵

補恤之惠若是者無乃論列愈詳而鹽法
愈不通耶屯政之不綜也始傷於嚴而卒
壞於寬也固習之故非一日矣自父祖侵
而有之而子孫固以爲巳世業也雖左驗
甚明至死不心服若是則雖有必行之政
安得而加哉富豪乾沒而告許橫行雖明
者或不能辨則仁者固不欲棘之也番休
之法不行兵久耗包依憑威虐兵實病民
田屯相遠形禁勢格兵不得田民亦病兵
punctuated:
商固四民之一，而職利之趨也，將使皇皇求仁義乎？商不近利，是農不望秋也。且買窩者奸商也，而賣窩者誰耶？不誅怯將而誅怯兵，兵益不精；不誅賄吏而誅賄民，賄益不止。法弊而售奸，良商亦奸；奸懲弊革，奸商亦良。人才與時奸良，而況商乎？別奸恤良，無以掊克之政一施之，則善矣。若夫括餘鹽之利，則京帑雖實，而邊郡增糴運之煩；加引目之數，則商利益微，而勤竈夫補恤之惠。若是者，無乃論列愈詳，而鹽法愈不通耶？

屯政之不綜也，始傷於嚴，而卒壞於寬也。因習之故，非一日矣。自父祖侵而有之，而子孫固以為巳世業也。雖左驗甚明，至死不心服。若是，則雖有必行之政，安得而加哉？富豪乾沒，而告訐横行，雖明者或不能辨，則仁者固不欲棘之也。番休之法不行，兵久駐屯，依憑威虐，兵實病民；田屯相遠，形勢勢格，兵不得田，民亦病兵。
translation_en:
Merchants are, after all, one of the four occupations, and their business is to pursue profit. Would one have them anxiously seek benevolence and righteousness? For merchants not to concern themselves with profit would be like farmers not to hope for an autumn harvest. Moreover, those who buy salt-trading entitlements are unscrupulous merchants, but who are those who sell them? Punish cowardly soldiers without punishing cowardly commanders, and the troops become still less effective; punish civilians who give bribes without punishing officials who take them, and bribery becomes still more persistent. When defective laws allow fraud to succeed, even honest merchants become dishonest; when fraud is punished and abuses reformed, even dishonest merchants become honest. Whether men of ability act dishonestly or honestly depends on their times—how much more so with merchants! Distinguish the dishonest and give consideration to the honest, rather than subjecting them all alike to policies of exaction: that would be good. As for appropriating the profits from surplus salt, this may fill the capital treasury, but it increases the burden of purchasing and transporting grain in the frontier commanderies. Increasing the number of salt certificates further reduces merchants’ profits and necessitates compensatory relief for the salt workers [?]. With measures such as these, is it not the case that the more detailed the deliberations become, the less workable the salt administration grows?

The failure to manage military agricultural colonies coherently began with the harm caused by excessive severity and ended with the ruin caused by excessive leniency. These entrenched practices did not arise in a single day. Fathers and grandfathers encroached upon the land and took possession of it; their descendants consequently regard it as their own hereditary property. Even when the corroborating evidence is perfectly clear, they will never acknowledge it in their hearts, even unto death. In such circumstances, even if a policy must be enforced, how can it be imposed upon them? The rich and powerful appropriate land, while accusations and denunciations run rampant. Even discerning men may be unable to distinguish the truth; benevolent men are therefore naturally unwilling to press the matter harshly. The system of rotational leave is not implemented, and soldiers remain stationed in the colonies for long periods, relying on their power to act oppressively: the soldiers truly afflict the people. The fields and the garrison settlements are far apart, and the terrain obstructs access [?]; the soldiers cannot obtain land, and the people in turn afflict the soldiers.

title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
當事者徒見其相成而不見其相濟則謂
屯田可罷清查可已殊不知天下無不弊
之法而有善通變之人宜早為之科制牢
以久之定限屯以遠近遞遷見存之田履
畝而定界服農之兵間歲而代更則亦庶
乎其可也張橫渠議井田朱考亭定經界
今之覈實屯田不猶差易於彼乎新屯之
增置立法之初固將有待于後來觀其分
數有定而置屯無限則可知矣其在南方
===
則凡荒山斥鹵之可墾淫溪祠毀寺之可
收者奸豪欺隱之可沒入者宜盡以為屯
田大江之北至于畿甸豈有不可勝用者
焉不然則近臣貴戚競請莊田於何取之
遠至于諸邊又有不可勝用者焉不然則
趙充國田金城韓重華田振武於何取之
且今兵籍向虛患人力之不足不患增屯
之無所田既增兵亦可□姑緩其舊而新
是圖不亦可乎夫科制不早定則將與見

當事者徒見其相成，而不見其相濟，則謂屯田可罷，清查可已。殊不知天下無不弊之法，而有善通變之人。宜早為之科制，牢以久之，定限屯以遠近遞遷，見存之田履畝而定界，服農之兵間歲而代更，則亦庶乎其可也。張橫渠議井田，朱考亭定經界，今之覈實屯田，不猶差易於彼乎？新屯之增置，立法之初固將有待于後來，觀其分數有定而置屯無限，則可知矣。

其在南方，則凡荒山斥鹵之可墾，淫溪祠毀寺之可收者，奸豪欺隱之可沒入者，宜盡以為屯田。大江之北至于畿甸，豈有不可勝用者焉？不然，則近臣貴戚競請莊田，於何取之？遠至于諸邊，又有不可勝用者焉。不然，則趙充國田金城，韓重華田振武，於何取之？且今兵籍向虛，患人力之不足，不患增屯之無所。田既增，兵亦可□。姑緩其舊，而新是圖，不亦可乎？夫科制不早定，則將與見
translation_en:
Those responsible see only how these reinforce one another, but fail to see how they might provide mutual assistance; they therefore say that military agricultural colonies can be abolished and investigations of their landholdings discontinued. They fail to understand that no system in the world is free from abuses, but there are people skilled at adapting it to changing circumstances. Regulations should be established promptly and made firm enough to endure. Limits should be set, and the colonies shifted in rotation according to their distance [?]. Existing fields should be surveyed plot by plot to determine their boundaries, and soldiers engaged in farming should be relieved in alternate years. Then the arrangement might prove workable. Zhang Hengqu proposed the well-field system, and Zhu Kaoting established land boundaries. Is verifying the actual holdings of military agricultural colonies today not somewhat easier than those undertakings? When the system was first instituted, the establishment of additional colonies was surely intended to await later action. This is evident from the fact that fixed proportions were prescribed, while no limit was imposed on the establishment of colonies.

In the south, all wasteland in the hills and saline land that can be reclaimed, land of unauthorized shrines and ruined monasteries that can be recovered [?], and land fraudulently concealed by unscrupulous local magnates that can be confiscated should be made into military agricultural land. North of the Great River, as far as the metropolitan region, could there not be more land than can be put to use? Otherwise, where would the estates come from that favored court officials and imperial relatives compete to request? Farther away, along the various frontiers, there is likewise more land than can be put to use. Otherwise, where did Zhao Chongguo obtain land to farm at Jincheng, or Han Chonghua at Zhenwu? Moreover, the military registers are now becoming depleted: the concern is insufficient manpower, not a lack of places in which to establish additional colonies. Once the farmland has increased, the soldiers too can be [illegible]. Might it not be possible to defer work on the old colonies for the time being and concentrate on the new? If regulations are not established promptly, then even the existing …

title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
存之額而并失新屯不增置則是棄可興
之利而他求若是者無乃清查愈密而屯
政愈不修耶嗚呼謀國之道何異理家理
家以衣食爲先而謀國以功利爲諱是心
也王耶霸耶談王而不知所以王及其無
策雖用霸術以救之亦無及矣我
祖宗勤民甚至而慮民甚深建置規畫損益近
代而良法美意三代同符是故食貨與師
八政之終始也山澤供賦地官之事守也
===
兵農兼務井地之遺教也且周人九職九
賦之法與夫任土之征取民之制甚輕而
斂財之途甚廣豈必取給於什一之稅哉
惟其廣斂財之途以寬經常之稅是以什
一行而頌聲作然則屯田鹽法之爲王者
之政可以灼然自信而無疑也彼以霸功
小視之者始而詿人終而誤國謀王斷國
者尚慎所决擇哉

punctuated: 存之額而并失，新屯不增置，則是棄可興之利而他求。若是者，無乃清查愈密而屯政愈不修耶？嗚呼！謀國之道何異理家？理家以衣食爲先，而謀國以功利爲諱，是心也，王耶？霸耶？談王而不知所以王，及其無策，雖用霸術以救之，亦無及矣！我祖宗勤民甚至，而慮民甚深，建置規畫，損益近代，而良法美意，三代同符。是故食貨與師，八政之終始也；山澤供賦，地官之事守也；兵農兼務，井地之遺教也。且周人九職九賦之法，與夫任土之征，取民之制甚輕，而斂財之途甚廣，豈必取給於什一之稅哉？惟其廣斂財之途，以寬經常之稅，是以什一行而頌聲作。然則屯田鹽法之爲王者之政，可以灼然自信而無疑也。彼以霸功小視之者，始而詿人，終而誤國。謀王斷國者，尚慎所决擇哉！
translation_en:
…even the existing quota will be lost along with it. If no new military agricultural colonies are established, this amounts to abandoning benefits that could be developed and seeking others elsewhere. If matters proceed thus, will it not be the case that the more meticulous the inspections become, the less effectively the colonies are administered?

Alas! How does managing a state differ from managing a household? In managing a household, one puts clothing and food first; yet in managing a state, one shuns discussion of practical achievement and material benefit. Is this the mind of a true king or of a hegemon? Those who speak of true kingship without understanding how to achieve it will eventually be left without a remedy. Even if they then employ the methods of a hegemon to rescue the situation, it will be too late!

Our imperial ancestors exerted themselves to the utmost for the people and considered their welfare most deeply. In their institutions and plans, they adapted the practices of more recent ages; yet their excellent laws and beneficent intentions accorded with those of the Three Dynasties. Thus food and wealth, together with military affairs, mark the beginning and end of the Eight Concerns of Government. Obtaining revenue from mountains and marshes was a charge of the officials of the Ministry of Education. Combining military service with farming was a teaching handed down from the well-field system.

Moreover, under the Zhou system of nine occupations and nine categories of levy, together with assessments based on the capabilities of the land, the prescribed exactions from the people were very light, while the sources from which revenue was gathered were very broad. Why should all needs have to be met from the tithe alone? Precisely because they broadened the sources of revenue so as to lighten regular taxation, the tithe could be implemented and songs of praise arose. We may therefore be clearly and confidently assured, without doubt, that military agricultural colonies and the salt administration are policies of true kingship. Those who belittle them as mere achievements of hegemony begin by misleading others and end by bringing the state into error. May those who devise plans for true kingship and decide affairs of state exercise care in their choices!

title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄後序
嘉靖甲午秋八月維應天府鄉
試臣以訓臣治受
上命往柄厥事旣行乃相與語曰兹
知人之哲也維艱哉曷弗懼旣
至適貢院落成制宏而麗森而
有域復相與語曰兹有司之理
===
也維共哉曷弗敬旣事事再旬
而竣錄成復相與語曰兹人文
之萃也維盛哉曷弗慶臣治敬
稽首拜言於其後曰夫錄有八
徵焉見
昭代之盛焉見
聖神之化焉見

嘉靖甲午秋八月維應天府鄉
試〔臣 臣〕〔詥 治〕受
上命往棫厥事既行乃相與語曰茲
知人之哲也維艱哉曷弗懼既
至適貢院落成制宏而麗森而

===
也維共哉曷弗敬既事事冉旬
而竣錄成復相與語曰茲人文
之萃也維盛哉曷弗慶〔臣 治〕〔詥 敬〕
稽首拜言於其後曰夫錄有八
徵焉見
昭代之盛焉見
聖神之化焉見
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄後序

嘉靖甲午秋八月，維應天府鄉試，臣以訓、臣治受上命往柄厥事。旣行，乃相與語曰：「兹知人之哲也，維艱哉！曷弗懼？」旣至，適貢院落成，制宏而麗，森而有域。復相與語曰：「兹有司之理也，維共哉！曷弗敬？」旣事，事再旬而竣，錄成。復相與語曰：「兹人文之萃也，維盛哉！曷弗慶？」臣治敬稽首拜言於其後曰：夫錄有八徵焉，見昭代之盛焉，見聖神之化焉，見
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the jiawu year of Jiajing [1534], on the occasion of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination, your servants Yixun and Zhi received His Majesty’s command to go and preside over its affairs. Having set out, we said to one another: “This calls for the wisdom to discern men’s worth. How difficult it is! How could we not feel apprehension?” Upon our arrival, the examination compound had just been completed. Its design was grand and beautiful, imposing and clearly partitioned. Again we said to one another: “This is the administrative work of the responsible officials. How dutifully it has been done! How could we not feel respect?” Once the work began, it was completed in twenty days, and the record was compiled. Again we said to one another: “Here is a gathering of literary cultivation. How flourishing it is! How could we not rejoice?” Your servant Zhi respectfully bows his head to the ground and offers these words at the end of the record: This record affords eight kinds of testimony. title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
王制之善焉見根本之重焉見都
會之美焉見道德之同焉見是
非之公焉見賓興之隆焉周公
而下道莫明於孔子而其學獨
盛於北其世運亦從而北時南
有荆楚之强孟軻而下道莫明
於周朱而其學獨盛於南其世
===

至於我

周公而下，道莫明於孔子，而其學獨盛於北，其世運亦從而北，時南有荆楚之强。孟軻而下，道莫明於周朱，而其學獨盛於南，其世運亦從而南，時北有胡元之亂。至於我朝，文教誕敷，訖於四海，詩書禮樂，蠻服咸暨，履中撫運，自生民以來未之能過焉。斯昭代之盛也。

translation_en:
…the excellence of royal institutions; it reveals the importance of the foundations, the splendor of the metropolis, the unity of the Way and virtue, the impartiality of judgments of right and wrong, and the flourishing of the ceremonial selection and advancement of worthy men.
Since the Duke of Zhou, no one elucidated the Way more clearly than Kongzi (Confucius). Yet his learning flourished especially in the north, and the fortunes of the age likewise followed it northward; at that time, the south was dominated by the power of Jing-Chu. Since Meng Ke (Mencius), no one elucidated the Way more clearly than Zhou Dunyi and Zhu Xi. Yet their learning flourished especially in the south, and the fortunes of the age likewise followed it southward; at that time, the north suffered the disorder of the non-Han Yuan dynasty. Under our dynasty, civilizing instruction has spread widely, reaching throughout the Four Seas. Poetry, documents, rites, and music have extended even to the distant lands of the barbarians. Holding to the Mean and presiding over the fortunes of the age, our dynasty has been unsurpassed since humankind first came into being. Such is the splendor of this illustrious age.
The means by which our imperial ancestors established the supreme standard and laid down models, thereby laying the foundation for a vast civilizing transformation…

translation_en:
…were most refined and thorough. For more than 160 years now, auspicious blessings have continued [?], and good government has thereby flourished. Our Emperor, with his grand plans and admirable standards, diligently sets an example. The worthy men among the people receive his virtuous influence; all spur themselves to render service and fulfill their duties as ministers [?]. Here is the spirit of the Odes “Luxuriant Southernwood” (Jing e) and “Oak Trees” (Yu pu), celebrating the nurturing of talent. Such is the transforming influence of our sagely and divine sovereign.
The selection and appointment of worthy men was a matter of great importance to the former kings. Later ages made additions and reductions, each adopting different institutions, but the essential aim was simply to obtain talented men to share in governing. Although the examination system established by our dynasty may seem unlike ancient practice, scholars who set their aspirations upon it are not diverted by other attractions. Thus men of exceptional talent all emerge through this system. With excellent counsel and far-reaching plans, they assist in government, and the altars of soil and grain depend upon them. Such is the excellence of the royal institutions.
In former times, King Wen attacked Chong and settled at Feng. Heaven’s…

title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
命用新而武王宅是鎬京四方
攸同乃昌燕翼以延八百之祀
我
太祖肇基金陵以混一海宇

大業而豐芑之懿寔首于茲土故

之言典以蓄朴以貞信以通物

translation_en:
…the Mandate was thereby renewed. King Wu then established his residence at Haojing, where the four quarters came together; thus he advanced plans for the welfare of his descendants, extending the dynasty’s ancestral sacrifices for eight hundred years. Our Taizu laid the foundations at Jinling, uniting all within the seas. Taizong established the dynasty’s enduring seat in Ji, occupying the central strategic position of the realm and securing the great enterprise for ten thousand generations. Yet the beneficent nurturing of successors, evoked by the luxuriant millet of the ode, began in this land. Thus the quotas for selecting scholars every three years are equally generous in the south and north: such is the importance of the foundations of the state.
Straddling the Huai and embracing Shu, commanding and linking Jing and Yue, this region is encircled by mountains and converging rivers, with fertile plains stretching a thousand li. It gathers spiritual potency and nurtures outstanding men, its accumulated brilliance growing ever greater. Its flourishing talents resemble carriage-illuminating pearls and munan gems shining in deep pools and vast marshes: their radiance cannot be concealed. Such is the excellence of this metropolitan region.
The scholars’ words are grounded in the classics and rich in substance, plain and steadfast, trustworthy and conversant with affairs. They clarify their aspirations so as to comprehend governance; in treating the guiding principles of human nature, Heaven’s decree, and the Kingly Way, they display refinement…

title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
彬爾非聖弗言焉斯道德之同
也詩弗愚者錄之易弗賊者錄
之書弗誣者錄之春秋弗亂者
錄之禮弗煩樂弗奢者錄之文
浮罔實弗錄也滯罔達弗錄也
僻罔正弗錄也故可以
獻可以傳可以程焉斯是非之公
===
也維
皇上懋學飭治以敬禮于邦國之賢
百辟祗若
休命修乃役罔有弗寅供億百陳
燕饗蠲備千夫馳庶工趨有司
程能咸曰茲政務之大斯賓興
之隆也然臣竊有憂焉錄公今

皇上懋學飭治以敬禮于邦國之賢
百辟祗若
休命修乃後罔有弗寅供億百停
燕饗蠲備千夫馳庶工趨有司

彬爾，非聖弗言焉，斯道德之同也。《詩》弗愚者錄之，《易》弗賊者錄之，《書》弗誣者錄之，《春秋》弗亂者錄之，《禮》弗煩、《樂》弗奢者錄之。文浮罔實弗錄也，滯罔達弗錄也，僻罔正弗錄也。故可以獻，可以傳，可以程焉，斯是非之公也。

translation_en:
…are refined and harmonious; they utter nothing that does not accord with the sages. Such is their shared commitment to the Way and virtue. Those whose treatment of the Book of Odes is free from foolishness are selected; those whose treatment of the Book of Changes is free from pernicious distortion are selected; those whose treatment of the Book of Documents is free from falsehood are selected; those whose treatment of the Spring and Autumn Annals is free from confusion are selected; and those whose treatment of the Rites is free from excessive complication and whose treatment of Music is free from extravagance are selected. Writing that is superficial and lacks substance is not selected; writing that is obstructed and lacks fluency is not selected; writing that is deviant and lacks correctness is not selected. Thus these writings may be presented to the throne, transmitted to posterity, and used as models. Such is the impartiality with which right and wrong are judged.
His Majesty diligently pursues learning and puts government in order, thereby showing reverence and courtesy to the worthy men of the realm. The officials reverently obey his gracious command and carry out their duties, none failing to act with respect. Supplies of every kind are laid out, and the banquets are prepared with scrupulous care. A thousand men hasten about, the various workers hurry to their tasks, and the responsible officials assess the candidates’ abilities. All declare that this is a great affair of government. Such is the honor accorded to the ceremonial reception and advancement of worthy men. Yet your servant privately harbors a concern: selection is impartial; now…

title: 嘉靖十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
庸有澤鞭以倖售者乎文同矣
庸有靜言而庸違者乎才美矣
庸有恃之而作狡者乎
制善矣庸有藉之以媒利者乎有
一於此將不重戾
聖王之教以自負
明時哉何以當畿域之勝耶其無
===
亦愧於有司之良爾矣是故君
子會盛以昌也淑化以養也軌
善以光也襲重以强也珍美以
章也若同以廣也篤公以揚也
昭隆以臧也察於此八者而主
之以道焉其用諸天下昭諸萬
世將無適而不宜夫是之謂才

punctuated:
庸有澤鞭以倖售者乎？文同矣，庸有靜言而庸違者乎？才美矣，庸有恃之而作狡者乎？制善矣，庸有藉之以媒利者乎？有一於此，將不重戾聖王之教，以自負明時哉？何以當畿域之勝耶？其無亦愧於有司之良爾矣！
是故君子會盛以昌也，淑化以養也，軌善以光也，襲重以强也，珍美以章也，若同以廣也，篤公以揚也，昭隆以臧也。察於此八者，而主之以道焉，其用諸天下，昭諸萬世，將無適而不宜。夫是之謂才
translation_en:
…could there be those who, like whips with a glossy exterior, hope through good fortune to find a buyer? Their writing conforms to the standard; could there be those whose words are agreeable but whose conduct is contrary? Their talents are fine; could there be those who rely on them to practise deceit? The regulations are good; could there be those who exploit them to secure private advantage? Anyone guilty of even one of these failings—would he not gravely contravene the sage king’s teachings and betray his own prospects in this enlightened age? How could he be worthy of the excellence of the metropolitan region? Would he not also feel shame before the fine officials responsible?
Thus the gentleman joins in flourishing achievement so as to prosper; receives beneficent transformation so as to nourish himself; follows goodness so as to shine; builds upon accumulated dignity so as to grow strong; treasures excellence so as to manifest it; accords with shared standards so as to broaden himself [?]; remains steadfast in impartiality so as to advance; and makes manifest what is exalted so as to attain goodness. By discerning these eight principles and governing them through the Way, he will find that, whether putting them into practice throughout the realm or displaying them to all succeeding ages, there is no circumstance in which they are unfitting. This is what is meant by talent…
